newsitem.title: UK: IBCA raises CORIFRANCE claims rating to A minus.
newsitem.headline: IBCA raises CORIFRANCE claims rating to A minus.

text.p: LONDON, Dec 20 - IBCA, the European credit rating agency, released the following statement on Friday.

IBCA has upgraded the Claims Settling Ability rating assigned to Compagnie de Reassurance d'Ile de France (CORIFRANCE) based in Paris, France from BBB plus (Adequate security) to A minus (Good security).

CORIFRANCE is a small reinsurer that writes predominantly short-tail business focusing on the "following lines" market. Approximately 75% of the account is Treaty business and the balance is Facultative business. Half of the company's business comes from Europe with the remainder split mainly between the Far East and North and Latin America.

The company maintains a conservative underwriting stance which is supported by good quality management and a high level of technical expertise. The risks accepted are mainly Property Damage and the company has no exposure to long-term US environmental pollution or industrial disease hazards.

The company strengthened its position in 1995 with strong underwriting and operating profits. Technical reserves were significantly below the market average level of the Association of French Reinsurers. However, IBCA considers these adequate in the light of past claims experience, the short-tail nature of the great majority of the business and the lack of US Liability exposure. Solvency benefited from the historically high earnings.

As a very small company, CORIFRANCE is more exposed to the negative effects of soft global reinsurance rates and consolidation of larger companies. IBCA does not anticipate significant premium growth in the immediate future and the company is expected to remain a small operator in its chosen niches. However, with no major losses reported for the 1995 and 1996 underwriting years to date, good results are expected for these years which should further enhance the financial profile.
